Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is the definition of long run?

options.A: the time period when all factors of production are specialised
options.B: the time period when all factors of production are variable
options.C: the time period when all key inputs into production are variable
options.D: the time period when at least one factor of production is fixed

questions.questionText: The table states the consequences of two macroeconomic policies. What correctly identifies whether the statements are normative or positive? a depreciation of an a rise in the minimum exchange rate will wage rate will cause cause the balance of unemployment to rise payments to improve

options.A: normative normative
options.B: normative positive
options.C: positive normative
options.D: positive positive

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the production possibility curve for wheat and corn. M output of wheat N O output of corn What can be deduced from the diagram?

options.A: As the price of corn falls, more of it is demanded.
options.B: Resources used in producing corn are more efficient than in producing wheat.
options.C: The opportunity cost of producing corn falls when moving from M to N.
options.D: The opportunity cost of producing corn is constant when moving from M to N.

questions.questionText: A supply curve is represented by the equation quantity supplied = 10 + 5P where P = the price of the product. Which price rise would cause the quantity supplied to double?

options.A: $1 to $2 B $1 to $3 C $1 to $4 D $1 to $5

questions.questionText: Which diagram illustrates unitary elasticity of supply?

options.A: B S S price price O O quantity quantity
options.C: D S price price S O O quantity quantity

questions.questionText: In which case is the price system not a possible method of allocating resources?

options.A: in the distribution of foodstuff among the population
options.B: in the hiring of workers by employers
options.C: in the ownership of land for agricultural use
options.D: in the provision of public goods by the government

questions.questionText: A sports stadium has two prices of seats. The cheaper seats are $10 and the more expensive seats are $20. When the prices of all seats are increased by 10%, the effects on demand are a fall of 5% for the cheaper seats and a fall of 12% for the more expensive seats. What describes the responsiveness of demand to the change in price? more expensive cheaper seats seats

options.A: elastic elastic
options.B: elastic inelastic
options.C: inelastic elastic
options.D: inelastic unitary elasticity

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes the shape of the demand curve for a normal good?

options.A: It shows an inverse relationship between income and quantity demanded.
options.B: It shows an inverse relationship between the price of the good and quantity demanded.
options.C: It shows a positive relationship between the price of the good and quantity demanded.
options.D: It shows a positive relationship between income and quantity demanded.

questions.questionText: Why does the basic economic problem of scarcity apply to both the rich and the poor?

options.A: The choices people make are not dependent on income inequalities.
options.B: Consumers pay the same prices for goods and services to satisfy their wants.
options.C: Human wants exceed what can be produced from available resources.
options.D: Natural resources are unevenly distributed amongst nations.

questions.questionText: Butter and buttermilk are goods in joint supply. Supply curves in both markets slope upwards to the right. Health concerns cause people to reduce their consumption of butter. What are the initial consequences of this for supply in the markets for butter and buttermilk? supply of butter supply of buttermilk

options.A: move left along supply curve move left along supply curve
options.B: move left along supply curve shift left of the supply curve
options.C: shift left of the supply curve move left along supply curve
options.D: shift left of the supply curve shift left of the supply curve

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply of a good. price S x P y D O Q quantity When the market is in equilibrium, which area measures the difference between what consumers are willing and able to pay and what producers receive at that output?

options.A: x B y C x + y D x – y

questions.questionText: Why do some local governments subsidise the provision of bicycles to encourage their use?

options.A: Consumers are afraid of having car accidents.
options.B: Consumers are unable to afford bicycles.
options.C: Consumers are not aware of the external benefits of using bicycles.
options.D: Consumers ignore the external costs of using bicycles.

questions.questionText: The table shows Gini coefficients for both income and wealth in two countries. country P country Q income 0.6 0.5 wealth 0.4 0.7 Which statement is correct?

options.A: Gini coefficients are not comparable between income and wealth because one is a flow concept and the other is a stock concept.
options.B: Income inequality is greater in country P than in country Q.
options.C: Wealth inequality is greater in country P than in country Q.
options.D: Wealth inequality is greater than income inequality in both countries.

questions.questionText: A government is faced with rising inflation. It wishes to reduce inflationary pressure while avoiding a fall in output. Which action is most likely to meet its needs?

options.A: an increase in laws to promote competition
options.B: an increase in taxation
options.C: an increase in the budget surplus
options.D: an increase in the exchange rate

questions.questionText: The table shows selected information from a country’s national accounts. $ billion GDP 28 net property income from abroad –3 capital consumption 6 national debt 2 What is the country’s net national income?

options.A: $19 billion B $25 billion C $31 billion D $33 billion

questions.questionText: The graphs show the changes in the exchange rates of the pound sterling (£) against the US dollar (US$) and the euro (€) between the years 2001 and 2003. US$ per £ £ per € 0.725 1.750 £ US$ 0.700 1.700 1.650 0.675 1.600 0.650 1.550 0.625 1.500 0.600 1.450 1.400 0.575 2001 2002 2003 2001 2002 2003 year year What happened to the value of the £ between the years 2001 and 2003?

options.A: The £ appreciated against the US$ and depreciated against the €.
options.B: The £ appreciated against the US$ and the €.
options.C: The £ depreciated against the US$ and appreciated against the €.
options.D: The £ depreciated against the US$ and the €.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the circular flow of income is correct?

options.A: Exports and imports do not affect the equilibrium level of national income because they always cancel each other out.
options.B: The greater the level of saving, the greater the level of injections in the form of investment must be.
options.C: When consumers use past savings to increase their spending, there will be a rise in national income.
options.D: When a government increases withdrawals by increasing the rate of income tax, there must be an equivalent increase in injections to compensate.

questions.questionText: The graph shows a country’s average annual inflation rate over a five-year period. average annual inflation rate (%) 0 year
In an economy, wages and prices are both rising but wages are rising faster. Which features are likely to exist in this economy? cost-push rise in real inflation incomes

options.A: no no
options.B: no yes
options.C: yes no
options.D: yes yes

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the aggregate demand (AD) and long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curves for a country. X is the original equilibrium position. In one year, over one million foreign workers left the country and at the same time the country’s currency appreciated against the currencies of its major trading partners. What will be the most likely new equilibrium position for this country? LRAS LRAS LRAS
What is most likely to cause a rise in a country’s exchange rate?

options.A: a fall in its direct taxes
options.B: a fall in its export orders
options.C: a rise in its interest rates
options.D: a rise in its imports

questions.questionText: Which change affecting the foreign exchange market for the US$ would be most likely to result in a shift to the right of the demand curve and a movement along the supply curve?

options.A: The US government reduces subsidies on exports to the EU.
options.B: Foreign currency speculators in Switzerland believe that the US$ is undervalued and act accordingly.
options.C: The US government intervenes in the foreign exchange market so as to bring about a drop in the value of the US$.
options.D: US pharmaceutical companies experience a fall in demand for their products from the rest of the world.

questions.questionText: What can be best understood from a knowledge of a country’s terms of trade?

options.A: its balance of payments performance
options.B: the purchasing power of its exports
options.C: the standard of living within the country
options.D: the value of its real exchange rate

questions.questionText: A company produces goods for export only. Which change could cause a rise in the price of its goods while the quantity sold is unchanged? domestic foreign workers’ consumers’ wages wages

options.A: unchanged fall
options.B: fall unchanged
options.C: fall fall
options.D: rise rise

questions.questionText: Under which current conditions will supply-side policy measures be most likely to achieve a country’s key macroeconomic goals? unemployment price level level

options.A: high stable
options.B: high rising
options.C: low stable
options.D: low rising

questions.questionText: Why might a government prefer to use floating exchange rates?

options.A: It allows the government more independence in policy making.
options.B: It encourages the government to build up its foreign exchange reserves.
options.C: It eliminates the instability of free markets.
options.D: It gives firms more confidence in future costs and prices.

questions.questionText: What is least likely to rise as a result of the use of expansionary fiscal policy?

options.A: aggregate demand
options.B: budget surplus
options.C: nominal income
options.D: inflation

questions.questionText: The table shows GDP indices for a country over a three-year period. year 1 year 2 year 3 real GDP 100 105 106 money GDP 100 107 115 Inflation and economic growth are two macroeconomic policy objectives. Which row gives a correct assessment of the country’s achievement of these two objectives over the period? rate of rate of inflation economic growth

options.A: cannot tell positive
options.B: declining cannot tell
options.C: positive declining
options.D: rising negative

options.A: a fall in domestic growth
options.B: consumer pessimism
options.C: increased domestic saving
